Revised assessment using the Financial Stability Report (FSR): The statement is hawkish—another 75 bp hike to a 3–3.25% range, guidance of “ongoing increases,” and continued balance-sheet reduction. The FSR around this period highlights vulnerabilities that tightening could expose: persistent Treasury and MBS liquidity strains, run-prone money market funds and stablecoins, elevated valuations, and rising interest-rate/credit risk in nonbanks, with Russia–Ukraine adding commodity and cyber risk. These factors tilt near-term risks to growth and market functioning more negative under tighter financial conditions. Offsetting this, the FSR notes banks are well capitalized with ample liquidity, the LIBOR-to-SOFR transition lowers benchmark risk, and standing facilities (RRP/repo) support market functioning—factors that reduce systemic tail risks. Net: hawkish with increased downside growth/market-liquidity risks but strong institutional backstops; overall slightly negative.
